Peyton Manning. An American football quarterback celebrated for his intelligence, accuracy, and record-breaking performances across an eighteen-season NFL career. Drafted first overall by the Indianapolis Colts in 1998, he led two franchises to Super Bowl victories and is the only quarterback to win championships with two different teams in the modern era. He spent his first fourteen seasons with the Colts and won a Super Bowl championship with them at Super Bowl XLI, then won a second with the Denver Broncos at Super Bowl fifty after the 2015 season. He earned fourteen Pro Bowl selections and won five NFL MVP awards, tying Wilt Chamberlain's record for the most in the modern era. He threw for seventy-one thousand nine hundred forty career passing yards and five hundred thirty-nine touchdowns, ranking among the all-time leaders and holding the record for most touchdown passes in a single season with fifty-five in 2013. He revolutionized the quarterback position through on-field audible calls and meticulous game preparation, becoming famous for his hand-signal Omaha snap calls. He endured a serious neck injury in 2011 that threatened his career but successfully recovered with the Colts before being released and joining Denver. He played professionally until 2015, achieving a second Super Bowl win at age thirty-nine in his final season.
